ios.desc:
Quick Issues is a native iOS issue capture app for developers who ship across GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Codeberg and self-hosted instances. Create issues in moments, organize everything in one unified inbox, and keep moving, even when you're offline.

CAPTURE IN SECONDS
Log a bug or an idea in a couple of seconds. No browser, no context switch.

ONE INBOX FOR EVERY REPO
Personal GitHub, work GitLab, a self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo instance, Codeberg. Connect them all and stop juggling tabs and logins. Forgejo and Codeberg are first-class, and the provider picker groups everything by hosting model, so connecting one is a couple of taps rather than a URL you have to look up.

ASSIGN WITHOUT LEAVING THE APP
Add or remove assignees on any issue, see who is on what from the list, and pull up everything assigned to you in a single view.

LINKED PULL REQUESTS
The pull requests that reference an issue show up on it automatically, colour-coded open, merged or closed. No tab switching to find out whether someone already fixed it.

OFFLINE FIRST
Capture on the subway, on a plane, on spotty hotel Wi-Fi. Quick Issues queues your changes and syncs them when you're back online.

BUILT FOR iOS 26
Pure native Swift. Not a web wrapper, not Electron. Markdown bodies render properly, including tables, task lists and fenced code. Labels stay readable in both appearances, and a ten-thousand-issue repo scrolls as smoothly as a ten-issue one.

Free: one account, unlimited repos.
Pro: multiple accounts, sync across devices.

Built by a solo developer who got tired of online-only apps on the subway.

quotes.text:
I got frustrated with how GitHub and GitLab's mobile apps handle issue creation. You need to be online, the flow is slow, and if you're on a self-hosted instance you're out of luck entirely.

So I built Quick Issues. It's a lightweight Swift app with an offline buffer -- you capture the issue, it syncs when you have connectivity. Supports GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea/Forgejo (including self-hosted and local with PAT).

A few technical notes for anyone interested: This was my first time using GRDB with SQLite instead of default Swift data structures, and the performance difference was significant. Setting up proper OAuth2 flows and GitHub/GitLab apps was more of an adventure than expected, but it's solid now.

Free for a single account/instance, paid tier if you juggle multiple providers.

My background is in GTD and data analytics, not traditional software engineering, so I'm genuinely curious: how does issue capture fit into your development workflow? Do you batch-create issues, capture them the moment they come up, use templates all the time or treat issues more as documentation only?
